issue: When a § 924(c) conviction rests on an unclear record about whether it was predicated on the residual clause, must the § 2255 movant show only that the conviction may have rested on the residual clause, or that it more likely than not did?

sides.position: A § 924(c) movant must show only that the conviction may have been predicated on the unconstitutional residual clause.
cases: United States v. Winston, 850 F.3d 677 (4th Cir. 2017)

sides.position: A § 924(c) movant must show that, more likely than not, the conviction resulted from application of solely the residual clause.
cases: Fernandez, 114 F.4th 1181 (circuit not identified in excerpt)
Barnes v. United States, No. 24-830 (2d Cir. 2025)

quote: As we acknowledged in Savoca I, “there is currently a circuit split as to a petitioner’s burden of proof where the sentencing record is ‘unclear’ as to which . . . clause an original sentencing court relied on.”
cite: Barnes v. United States, No. 24-830 (2d Cir. 2025)
